newsitem.title: UK: Greycoat rejects portfolio break-up attempt.
newsitem.headline: Greycoat rejects portfolio break-up attempt.

text.p: British property company Greycoat Plc said on Monday that a resolution tabled by dissident shareholders to liquidate its portfolio was ill-conceived and would fail to secure shareholder value.
The company said it had posted a circular to shareholders recommending they vote against the resolution, which is due to be proposed at an extraordinary general meeting on November 14.
Greycoat chairman Michael Beckett said in a statement that the company's portfolio of "well-located central London buildings and developments" would all be completed within the next two years.
It was therefore "well positioned to take advantage of the improving market and generate additional profits free of tax".

The company said the total liquidation of the portfolio, as demanded by the UK Active Value Fund, IMP UKAV Inc and Chaddesley Investments Limited, would sacrifice inherent growth potential and development surpluses.

It also disregarded the negative impact on prices of a so-called "closing-down sale" and ignored the effect on net proceeds of transaction costs, penalties for prematurely closing out hedged financing and the benefit of the group's tax shield.

Greycoat said its progress was clearly demonstrated by its results for the six months to September 30, 1996. These showed an increase in pretax profits of 123 percent to 3.8 million stg and an increase in earnings per share of 138 percent to 3.1 pence. It also expects to pay a dividend for the year as a whole of 1.2 pence net per share.
Greycoat warned shareholders that if they did not vote against the resolution, it could be "passed by default".
